To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) family support is a protective factor for depression and suicide in adolescence, 2) the 5 HTTLDR gene is associated with adolescent depression and suicide, and 3) there is a significant interaction between the 5 HTLPR gene and family support on adolescent depression and suicide risk.
the serotonin transporter linked polymorphic region (5 HTTLRP) gene interacts with family support in the prediction of depression symptoms and suicidal behavior in adolescents.

(a) the serotonin transporter gene moderates the association between family cohesion, communication, warmth and adolescent depression and suicide risk; (b) the association is moderated by the presence of the short allele; (c) the association between family support and depression is stronger in the presence of the long allele, but only for girls; (d) the association between the presence of the 5 HTTLRP short allele and adolescent depression is stronger in boys with poor family cohesion, communication and warmth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of depressive disorders and suicidal behavior.
the role of the serotonin transporter gene (5 HTT) in the development of depressive disorders and suicidal behaviors.
the interplay of environmental and genetic factors in the development of psychopathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 5 HTTLP gene is not associated with the risk of developing depression or suicide in the presence of good quality family support, but that it may be a risk factor in the presence of poor quality family support, and may also be protective in the presence of very high quality family support.
the short allele of the 5-HTTLPR gene interacts with family support to influence the risk for adolescent depression and suicidal behavior.
the short allele in the 5HTTLPR may be differentially sensitive to family environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the short allele is a risk factor for depression and suicide in the presence of poor family support.
family support is an important factor in the development of youth depression and suicidality.
family support is an important environmental factor for adolescent depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
family support is a protective factor against adolescent depression, but the effect of family support is moderated by genotype.
the interaction between the 5HTTLPR and family cohesion is a significant predictor of depression symptoms and risk of suicide attempts in boys.
family support is important for all youth and may be particularly important for youth with the short allele of the serotonin transporter gene.
